items.item_text: 01. Information I provide to the following supplemental questions will be reviewed as part of the application process. Questions that are not fully and completely answered will be considered grounds for disqualification from the examination process. Stating "see resume" in lieu of a complete response to these questions is not acceptable. Select "Yes" to indicate that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes
02. Do you have a high school diploma or equivalent? Options: Yes | No
03. Does your education include college-level coursework or training in statistical analysis, testing or data base management? Options: Yes | No

04. If you answered "Yes" to the previous question: Please list the college-level coursework and/or training in statistical analysis, testing or data base management or related field below. If you answered "No": Please enter "N/A" below.

05. How many years of verifiable, job related experience involving student test score data base management and computer systems does your application demonstrate? Options: Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 3-4 years | 5 years or more

06. How many years of verifiable, job related experience in testing administration, including explaining testing procedures or carrying out changes to testing methods does you application demonstrate? Options: Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 3-4 years | 5 years or more

07. According to the job announcement, check the box that most closely matches your level of proficiency to perform the minimum qualifications listed: Training and providing work direction to assigned staff. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

08. Developing and maintaining records, and generating reports based on the data collected. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

09. Interpreting and applying federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations concerning the coordination, preparation, distribution, collection and scoring of numerous State-mandated tests. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations.. | Proficient in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

10. Select the option that indicates your level of proficiency with MS Office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS Outlook, MS Powerpoint). Options: None. I have no experience in working with Microsoft Office software products. | Beginner. Perform daily word processing tasks in Word, enter correct data, create a database, format cells, rows and columns in Excel; create a PowerPoint presentation file with a title slide, bullet points and place in slide loop mode; create a new email message, checking email in Outlook. | Intermediate. Basic formatting and create a variety of templates, mail merges in Word; create, modify and format charts, use graphic objects to enhance worksheets and charts in Excel; add special effects to presentation (design and animation) in PowerPoint; reply, forward, print and delete email messages in Outlook. | Advanced. Manage table data, sort and filter merges in Word; use the filter and formula functions to manipulate data in Excel; transition presentation slides, link Excel charts to presentation and add voice in PowerPoint; delete e-mails from the Inbox, Sent Items and Deleted Items folders, add, edit, move and delete appointments on your calendar in Outlook. | Expert. Produce table of contents, footnotes, endnotes, bookmarks in Word; use advance formula functions, manage macro commands, group rows in Excel; publish presentation online, embed objects into presentation in PowerPoint; manage multiple calendars, set rules for incoming mail, create subfolders for mail to be placed in Outlook.

11. Describe your knowledge and work related experience using the student information systems and testing operations management systems. Be sure to list the names of such systems and the level of expertise you have using each one.
12. Briefly describe a time you provided excellent customer service in the administration of a test. What steps did you take? What problems did you encounter and how did you overcome them?

13. Using examples from your work history, discuss a situation you faced that highlights your strengths in problem solving, organization and follow-through. What was the situation and how did your skills lead to a positive outcome?

ESSENTIAL DUTIES: Plan, organize, coordinate and implement specialized duties in support of the District student assessment program; serve as a technical resource to school sites, system vendors, subcontractors, auditors and parents regarding assessment policies and procedures and data information. Coordinate state testing aspects including ordering, training, assisting with compliance, maintaining testing procedures and security; provide administrative support and oversight to current state testing standards and physical fitness tests. Provide support to District-level assessments; design assessment shells and other data collection and reporting systems. Maintain the data warehouse, student information system and associated reports; import external and State test data; maintain data integrity; create accounts and provide school site support; create data reports to assist with the identification of trends and support of instructional initiatives. Provide support to State accountability reports; compile and create data reports; review CALPADS extracts to assure data integrity. Train and provide work direction to assigned staff. Provide technical information and assistance to the Director regarding assigned functions; assist in the formulation and development of policies, procedures and programs. Prepare and maintain a variety of narrative and statistical reports, records and files related to personnel and assigned activities. Communicate with other administrators, personnel and outside organizations to coordinate activities and programs, resolve issues and conflicts and exchange information. Participate in the development of the annual preliminary budget; analyze and review budgetary and financial data; control and authorize expenditures in accordance with established limitations. Operate a computer and assigned software programs; operate other office equipment as assigned. Attend and conduct a variety of meetings as assigned. OTHER DUTIES: Perform related duties as assigned.

Planning, organization, coordination and implementation of specialized duties in support of a student assessment program. State assessment codes and policies. Elementary and secondary education terminology. Oral and written communication skills. Principles and practices of supervision and training. Applicable laws, codes, regulations, policies and procedures. Interpersonal skills using tact, patience and courtesy. Operation of a computer and assigned software.

Plan, organize, coordinate and implement specialized duties in support of the District student assessment program. Coordinate state testing aspects including ordering, training, assisting with compliance, maintaining testing procedures and security. Provide support to District-level assessments. Maintain the data warehouse, student information system and associated reports. Provide support to State accountability reports. Train provide work direction to assigned staff. Communicate effectively both orally and in writing. Interpret, apply and explain rules, regulations, policies and procedures. Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others. Operate a computer and assigned office equipment. Analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action. Meet schedules and time lines. Work independently with little direction. Plan and organize work. Maintain records and files. Prepare comprehensive narrative and statistical reports.
